title: Last Stone Loses (Misère Nim)
description:
Alice and Bob play Nim with a twist. There are several piles of stones. On a turn, a player picks one non-empty pile and removes any positive number of stones from it. The player who takes the last stone overall loses. Alice moves first and both play optimally. Answer this for T independent games.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ T ≤ 1000
  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105 piles per game; the total number of piles over all games is at most 2·105
  • 1 ≤ ai ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains T. Each game is described by a line with n followed by a line with n integers a1 ... an.

Output

For each game print Alice if the first player wins, otherwise Bob, one per line.

Example

Input:

4
2
1 1
3
1 1 1
2
2 2
3
1 2 3

Output:

Alice
Bob
Bob
Bob
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    t = int(d[0]); p = 1; out = []
    for _ in range(t):
        n = int(d[p]); p += 1
        x = 0; big = False
        for v in d[p:p + n]:
            v = int(v); x ^= v
            if v > 1: big = True
        p += n
        if big:
            out.append("Alice" if x else "Bob")
        else:
            out.append("Alice" if n % 2 == 0 else "Bob")
    print("\n".join(out))
main()

title: Staircase Nim: Count Winning Moves
description:
A staircase has steps numbered 1..n (step 0 is the floor). Step i holds ci coins. On a turn, a player chooses a step i ≥ 1 with at least one coin and moves any positive number of its coins down to step i - 1. Coins on the floor can never move again. The player who cannot move loses. Alice moves first; both play optimally.

If Alice wins, also count her winning first moves: the number of distinct pairs (i, k) (move k coins from step i) after which Bob is in a losing position.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105
  • 0 ≤ ci ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains n; the second line contains c1 ... cn.

Output

Print Bob if Bob wins. Otherwise print Alice W where W is the number of winning first moves.

Example

Input:

3
1 2 3

Output:

Alice 2

title: Fence Posts and Fields (Pick's Theorem)
description:
A farmer's field is a simple polygon (edges do not cross or touch except at shared endpoints of consecutive edges) whose vertices are lattice points. Compute three things:

  • the area of the polygon, printed exactly (it is always a multiple of 0.5), with one decimal: e.g. 12.0 or 7.5;
  • B: the number of lattice points on the boundary;
  • I: the number of lattice points strictly inside.

Vertices may be given clockwise or counterclockwise, and some vertices may lie on the straight line through their neighbours.

Constraints

  • 3 ≤ n ≤ 105
  • |x|, |y| ≤ 106
  • Floating point answers will be wrong — use integer arithmetic.

Input

The first line contains n. The next n lines contain the vertices x y in order along the boundary.

Output

Print A B I on one line, separated by spaces.

Example

Input:

4
0 0
4 0
4 3
0 3

Output:

12.0 14 6
solution:
import sys
from math import gcd
d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(); n = int(d[0])
xs = list(map(int, d[1:2 * n + 1:2])); ys = list(map(int, d[2:2 * n + 2:2]))
s = 0; b = 0
for i in range(n):
    x1, y1 = xs[i - 1], ys[i - 1]; x2, y2 = xs[i], ys[i]
    s += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
    b += gcd(x2 - x1, y2 - y1)
s = abs(s)
inner = (s - b + 2) // 2
print(f"{s // 2}.{5 if s % 2 else 0} {b} {inner}")

title: Two Piles, Diagonal Moves (Wythoff's Game)
description:
Two piles hold a and b stones. A move is one of: remove any positive number of stones from one pile, or remove the same positive number of stones from both piles. The player who cannot move loses (so the player who empties both piles wins). Alice moves first and both play optimally.

For each query, print the number of winning first moves for Alice: moves after which Bob is in a losing position. A move is identified by the resulting pair (a', b') (pile order matters). Print 0 if Alice loses.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ Q ≤ 2000
  • 0 ≤ a, b ≤ 1018
  • Double-precision golden-ratio formulas lose accuracy near 1018; use exact integer arithmetic (e.g. math.isqrt).

Input

The first line contains Q; each of the next Q lines contains a b.

Output

Print the Q answers on one line, separated by spaces.

Example

Input:

5
0 0
1 2
1 1
3 5
4 4

Output:

0 0 1 0 1
solution:
import sys
from math import isqrt
def A(k): return (k + isqrt(5 * k * k)) // 2
def partner(v):
    if v == 0: return 0
    k0 = (isqrt(5 * v * v) - v) // 2
    for k in range(max(1, k0 - 2), k0 + 3):
        if A(k) == v: return v + k
    k0 = (3 * v - isqrt(5 * v * v)) // 2
    for k in range(max(1, k0 - 2), k0 + 3):
        if A(k) + k == v: return A(k)
    raise ValueError
d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(); q = int(d[0]); out = []
for i in range(q):
    a = int(d[1 + 2 * i]); b = int(d[2 + 2 * i])
    lo, hi = min(a, b), max(a, b)
    if A(hi - lo) == lo:
        out.append(0); continue
    w = 0
    if partner(a) < b: w += 1
    if partner(b) < a: w += 1
    if A(hi - lo) < lo: w += 1
    out.append(w)
print(*out)

title: Token Game on a Directed Graph
description:
A token sits on a node of a directed graph (cycles, self-loops and repeated edges are allowed). Players alternate moving the token along one outgoing edge. A player who cannot move loses. If play can go on forever under optimal play (a player who would lose prefers an infinite game, and a player who can force a win does so), the result is a draw.

Classify every node as W (the player to move wins), L (the player to move loses) or D (draw), then answer queries.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 105, 0 ≤ m ≤ 2·105
  • 1 ≤ Q ≤ 3000
  • Repeatedly re-scanning all nodes until nothing changes is too slow; use retrograde analysis (BFS backwards from terminal nodes).

Input

The first line contains n m. The next m lines contain edges u v (from u to v, 1-based). Then a line with Q and a line with Q node numbers.

Output

Line 1: the number of W, L and D nodes, separated by spaces. Line 2: a string of Q characters, the classification of each queried node in order.

Example

Input:

4 3
1 2
2 3
3 4
4
1 2 3 4

Output:

2 2 0
WLWL
solution:
import sys
from collections import deque
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, m = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    rev = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    deg = [0] * (n + 1)
    p = 2
    for _ in range(m):
        u = int(d[p]); v = int(d[p + 1]); p += 2
        rev[v].append(u); deg[u] += 1
    res = [0] * (n + 1)  # 0 undecided, 1 W, 2 L
    dq = deque()
    for v in range(1, n + 1):
        if deg[v] == 0:
            res[v] = 2; dq.append(v)
    while dq:
        v = dq.popleft()
        rv = res[v]
        for u in rev[v]:
            if res[u]: continue
            if rv == 2:
                res[u] = 1; dq.append(u)
            else:
                deg[u] -= 1
                if deg[u] == 0:
                    res[u] = 2; dq.append(u)
    ch = "DWL"
    w = res.count(1); l = res.count(2)
    q = int(d[p]); qs = d[p + 1:p + 1 + q]
    print(w, l, n - w - l)
    print("".join(ch[res[int(x)]] for x in qs))
main()

title: Fence Around the Orchard (Convex Hull)
description:
Given n trees as lattice points (duplicates possible), output the vertices of their convex hull. Points lying on a hull edge but not at a corner are not vertices. Print the vertices in counterclockwise order starting from the vertex with the smallest y (ties: smallest x).

Degenerate cases: if all points coincide, the hull is that single point; if all points are collinear, the hull is the two extreme points (start with the one with smaller y, ties by smaller x).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
  • |x|, |y| ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains n; each of the next n lines contains x y.

Output

First print h, the number of hull vertices, then h lines x y.

Example

Input:

6
0 0
2 0
1 1
2 2
0 2
1 0

Output:

4
0 0
2 0
2 2
0 2
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(); n = int(d[0])
    pts = sorted(set(zip(map(int, d[1:2 * n + 1:2]), map(int, d[2:2 * n + 2:2]))))
    if len(pts) == 1:
        print(1); print(*pts[0]); return
    def build(seq):
        h = []
        for p in seq:
            while len(h) >= 2:
                o, a = h[-2], h[-1]
                if (a[0] - o[0]) * (p[1] - o[1]) - (a[1] - o[1]) * (p[0] - o[0]) <= 0:
                    h.pop()
                else:
                    break
            h.append(p)
        return h
    lo = build(pts); up = build(pts[::-1])
    hull = lo[:-1] + up[:-1]
    s = min(range(len(hull)), key=lambda i: (hull[i][1], hull[i][0]))
    hull = hull[s:] + hull[:s]
    print(len(hull))
    print("\n".join(f"{x} {y}" for x, y in hull))
main()

title: Inside the Convex Fortress
description:
A fortress wall is a strictly convex polygon with n lattice vertices given in counterclockwise order (no three vertices collinear). For each of Q scouts, decide whether the scout is strictly inside, on the wall (boundary, including vertices), or outside.

Constraints

  • 3 ≤ n ≤ 105, 1 ≤ Q ≤ 6·104
  • |x|, |y| ≤ 109
  • O(n) per query is too slow; answer each query in O(log n).

Input

The first line contains n, followed by n lines with vertices x y. Then a line with Q, followed by Q lines with query points x y.

Output

Print three integers: the number of scouts strictly inside, on the boundary, and outside.

Example

Input:

4
0 0
4 0
4 4
0 4
6
2 2
4 2
0 0
5 5
4 5
1 3

Output:

2 2 2
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(); n = int(d[0])
    X = list(map(int, d[1:2 * n + 1:2])); Y = list(map(int, d[2:2 * n + 2:2]))
    p = 2 * n + 1; q = int(d[p]); p += 1
    x0, y0 = X[0], Y[0]
    ax = [x - x0 for x in X]; ay = [y - y0 for y in Y]
    ins = bnd = out = 0
    for t in range(q):
        qx = int(d[p]) - x0; qy = int(d[p + 1]) - y0; p += 2
        c1 = ax[1] * qy - ay[1] * qx
        cn = ax[n - 1] * qy - ay[n - 1] * qx
        if c1 < 0 or cn > 0:
            out += 1; continue
        lo, hi = 1, n - 2
        while lo < hi:
            mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
            if ax[mid] * qy - ay[mid] * qx >= 0: lo = mid
            else: hi = mid - 1
        l = lo
        c = (ax[l + 1] - ax[l]) * (qy - ay[l]) - (ay[l + 1] - ay[l]) * (qx - ax[l])
        if c < 0: out += 1
        elif c == 0: bnd += 1
        elif (c1 == 0 and l == 1) or (cn == 0 and l == n - 2): bnd += 1
        else: ins += 1
    print(ins, bnd, out)
main()

title: Closest Pair of Beacons
description:
Given n beacons at lattice points (two beacons may share a location), find the minimum squared Euclidean distance between two different beacons.

Constraints

  • 2 ≤ n ≤ 5·104
  • |x|, |y| ≤ 109
  • O(n2) is too slow, and so is a sweep that only prunes by x when many points share an x; use divide and conquer (or an equivalent O(n log n) method).

Input

The first line contains n; each of the next n lines contains x y.

Output

Print the minimum squared distance as an integer.

Example

Input:

4
0 0
3 4
10 10
1 1

Output:

2
solution:
import sys
def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(10000)
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(); n = int(d[0])
    pts = sorted(zip(map(int, d[1:2 * n + 1:2]), map(int, d[2:2 * n + 2:2])))
    for i in range(n - 1):
        if pts[i] == pts[i + 1]:
            print(0); return
    best = [(pts[0][0] - pts[1][0]) ** 2 + (pts[0][1] - pts[1][1]) ** 2]
    def rec(lo, hi):
        if hi - lo <= 3:
            sub = pts[lo:hi]
            b = best[0]
            for i in range(len(sub)):
                for j in range(i + 1, len(sub)):
                    v = (sub[i][0] - sub[j][0]) ** 2 + (sub[i][1] - sub[j][1]) ** 2
                    if v < b: b = v
            best[0] = b
            return sorted(sub, key=lambda p: p[1])
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        mx = pts[mid][0]
        left = rec(lo, mid); right = rec(mid, hi)
        merged = sorted(left + right, key=lambda p: p[1])
        b = best[0]
        strip = [p for p in merged if (p[0] - mx) ** 2 < b]
        ln = len(strip)
        for i in range(ln):
            x1, y1 = strip[i]
            j = i + 1
            while j < ln:
                x2, y2 = strip[j]
                dy = y2 - y1
                if dy * dy >= b: break
                v = (x2 - x1) ** 2 + dy * dy
                if v < b: b = v
                j += 1
        best[0] = b
        return merged
    rec(0, n)
    print(best[0])
main()

title: Area Covered by Tarps
description:
Workers lay n axis-aligned rectangular tarps on the ground; they may overlap. Compute the total area covered by at least one tarp.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 5000
  • 0 ≤ x1 < x2 ≤ 109, 0 ≤ y1 < y2 ≤ 109
  • The answer can exceed 64-bit floating-point precision; compute it exactly. Re-merging intervals for every vertical strip is too slow; use a sweep line with a segment tree over compressed coordinates.

Input

The first line contains n. Each of the next n lines contains x1 y1 x2 y2 (opposite corners).

Output

Print the covered area as an integer.

Example

Input:

2
0 0 2 2
1 1 3 3

Output:

7
solution:
import sys
def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(10000)
    d = list(map(int, sys.stdin.buffer.read().split())); n = d[0]
    ev = []; ys = set()
    for i in range(n):
        x1, y1, x2, y2 = d[1 + 4 * i:5 + 4 * i]
        ev.append((x1, 1, y1, y2)); ev.append((x2, -1, y1, y2))
        ys.add(y1); ys.add(y2)
    ys = sorted(ys); idx = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(ys)}
    m = len(ys) - 1
    cnt = [0] * (4 * m + 4); ln = [0] * (4 * m + 4)
    def upd(node, l, r, ql, qr, v):
        if qr <= l or r <= ql: return
        if ql <= l and r <= qr:
            cnt[node] += v
        else:
            mid = (l + r) // 2
            upd(2 * node, l, mid, ql, qr, v); upd(2 * node + 1, mid, r, ql, qr, v)
        if cnt[node]: ln[node] = ys[r] - ys[l]
        elif r - l == 1: ln[node] = 0
        else: ln[node] = ln[2 * node] + ln[2 * node + 1]
    ev.sort()
    area = 0; px = ev[0][0]
    for x, t, y1, y2 in ev:
        area += ln[1] * (x - px); px = x
        upd(1, 0, m, idx[y1], idx[y2], t)
    print(area)
main()

title: Most Stars in a Straight Line
description:
Given n stars at lattice points, find the largest number of stars lying on one straight line. Stars may share the same position (each counts separately), and any single star or pair of stars always lies on some line.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 800
  • |x|, |y| ≤ 109
  • Comparing slopes as floats gives wrong answers; normalize direction vectors with gcd. O(n3) is too slow.

Input

The first line contains n; each of the next n lines contains x y.

Output

Print the maximum number of stars on one line.

Example

Input:

5
1 1
2 2
3 3
1 2
0 5

Output:

3
solution:
import sys
from math import gcd
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(); n = int(d[0])
    X = list(map(int, d[1:2 * n + 1:2])); Y = list(map(int, d[2:2 * n + 2:2]))
    best = 1
    for i in range(n):
        xi, yi = X[i], Y[i]
        cnt = {}; dup = 0; mx = 0
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            dx = X[j] - xi; dy = Y[j] - yi
            if dx == 0 and dy == 0:
                dup += 1; continue
            g = gcd(dx, dy); dx //= g; dy //= g
            if dx < 0 or (dx == 0 and dy < 0): dx = -dx; dy = -dy
            k = (dx, dy)
            c = cnt.get(k, 0) + 1; cnt[k] = c
            if c > mx: mx = c
        if mx + dup + 1 > best: best = mx + dup + 1
    print(best)
main()

title: Counting Right Triangles
description:
Given n distinct lattice points, count the number of unordered triples of points that form a non-degenerate right triangle (one angle exactly 90°).

Constraints

  • 3 ≤ n ≤ 600
  • |x|, |y| ≤ 109
  • O(n3) is too slow. For each point as the right-angle vertex, group the other points by normalized direction and match perpendicular directions.

Input

The first line contains n; each of the next n lines contains x y.

Output

Print the number of right triangles.

Example

Input:

4
0 0
1 0
0 1
1 1

Output:

4
solution:
import sys
from math import gcd
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(); n = int(d[0])
    X = list(map(int, d[1:2 * n + 1:2])); Y = list(map(int, d[2:2 * n + 2:2]))
    total = 0
    for i in range(n):
        xi, yi = X[i], Y[i]
        cnt = {}
        for j in range(n):
            if j == i: continue
            dx = X[j] - xi; dy = Y[j] - yi
            g = gcd(dx, dy)
            k = (dx // g, dy // g)
            cnt[k] = cnt.get(k, 0) + 1
        for (dx, dy), c in cnt.items():
            o = cnt.get((-dy, dx))
            if o: total += c * o
    print(total)
main()

title: Cutting Branches (Green Hackenbush on Trees)
description:
A garden has a forest of rooted trees. Node i hangs from its parent pi by a branch; if pi = 0, node i is a root and its branch is attached to the ground. So there are exactly n branches, one above every node.

Players alternate cutting one remaining branch. After a cut, everything no longer connected to the ground (the whole subtree below the cut branch) disappears. The player who cannot cut loses. Alice moves first; both play optimally.

If Alice wins, also count her winning first moves (the number of branches whose cut leaves Bob in a losing position).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105
  • The parent pointers form a forest (no cycles). Parents may have larger indices than children; trees can be very deep (use iteration, not recursion).

Input

The first line contains n. The second line contains p1 ... pn.

Output

Print Bob if Bob wins, otherwise Alice W.

Example

Input:

3
0 1 1

Output:

Alice 1
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split(); n = int(d[0])
    par = [0] + [int(v) for v in d[1:n + 1]]
    ch = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for v in range(1, n + 1):
        ch[par[v]].append(v)
    order = [0]
    for v in order:
        order.extend(ch[v])
    g = [0] * (n + 1)
    for v in reversed(order):
        x = 0
        for c in ch[v]: x ^= g[c] + 1
        g[v] = x
    if g[0] == 0:
        print("Bob"); return
    need = [-1] * (n + 1); need[0] = 0
    w = 0
    for v in order:
        if need[v] < 0: continue
        base = need[v] ^ g[v]
        for c in ch[v]:
            x = base ^ (g[c] + 1)
            if x == 0: w += 1
            else: need[c] = x - 1
    print("Alice", w)
main()
